subject: law
title: General
intro: A map of the supplied Maturita 2026 oral-examination themes. This document specifies scope; it does not supply complete explanations for all twenty-one themes.

blocks.text: The syllabus moves from the foundations and institutions of law to criminal justice, evidence and the interpretation of cases. Use these connections to organise revision: knowing a definition is different from explaining how it operates in a dispute.

items: Themes 1–5: common-law history, the rule of law, American law, courts and landmark decisions.
Themes 6–8: international law, human-rights conflicts and civil disputes.
Themes 9–14: criminal law, criminal justice, juries, police, lawyers and punishment.
Themes 15–21: forensic and testimonial evidence, interviewing and interrogation, offender profiling, case studies and current events.

blocks.text: The date and title belong to the supplied 2026 syllabus. Availability of a theme in this list does not mean that its teaching materials are already present here.

lessons.title: Connect a case to its institutions and evidence

blocks.text: A useful revision route is to choose a listed case-study theme, identify the legal category involved, explain which legal people and courts participate, then identify what kind of evidence matters. This is a study method inferred from the syllabus structure, not a new examination requirement.

steps.title: Locate the theme
steps.text: Identify the relevant numbered theme in the syllabus.

steps.title: Connect the concepts
steps.text: Relate it to foundations, procedure, institutions or evidence in another listed theme.

steps.title: Check the source coverage
steps.text: Return to the actual teaching material before adding specific legal rules or case outcomes.
